key_insight: PING uses a physics-informed graph neural network to forecast transport dynamics on irregular sensor networks and improve intra-day solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-motion and PV production forecasts can support grid integration of solar power rather than directly improve solar cell efficiency.
method: Represent advection–diffusion particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground sensors and satellite cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical gains or deployment costs, so practical forecasting benefits and computational requirements need further assessment.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
